description: Hilbert–Schmidt matrix-O probe (PR #4064 Frobenius-pairing lens): does the MATRIX Gram-resolvent ⟨O,(G−μ)⁻¹O⟩=tr(Oᵀ(G−μ)⁻¹O) supply the bar-odd flip the SCALAR Frobenius closure Σy_λχ_λΔ_λ cannot? O = fig-8 (σ₀σ₁⁻¹)² left-reg rep on the H₃(q) NF basis; G = canonical Markov Gram; μ geometric (0/1/z/λ_min−ε), no fit. FINDINGS (scope-(a)): (1) NO sign flip at any μ — HS(p)/HS(m)≈+1.0000 vs target −4.08, incl. near-pole μ (mag ~1e6, same sign). (2) The pairing is BAR-EVEN (|HS(q)−HS(1/q)|≪|HS(q)+HS(1/q)|); S is bar-ODD (Lean fig8Trace_im_odd), so a real bar-even resolvent from Markov (bar-even) data cannot carry S's chirality. (3) Gram eigenvalues shift ~1e-8 same-direction, no crossing; a fixed μ between anchors would be a ~1e-8 fit AND diverge (pole) not zero-cross. A REAL matrix resolvent alone does not reproduce bar-odd S — reconfirms the proved bar-parity obstruction from a matrix direction. NOT scope-(b) for a COMPLEX fibre-level pole; surviving open object = pole→cusp phase φ(q₀) (qbeta_c3_barodd_pole_cusp_phase_probe.py), the fibre continuation that is the c₃⟺q₀ crux bwS0_eq_hecke. No fit; nothing wired; no tier change.
